tools.description: Unsigned transactions. Without account: open a line owned by the signing wallet for an agent (never the wallet itself), in a market credit_markets lists ("CREDIT", the default), post its credits and optionally borrow USDG at once (to the wallet unless to names an allowlisted address); exact credit approval to the factory first. The owner's limits: ceiling (USDG, default the most the target allows today), daily_limit (USDG out in any 24 hours, borrows and the agent's withdrawals together, or "none"; default the ceiling, or $100 with a gas station; at most $5,000 with one), target_ltv (a fraction under 1 like 0.18, or a percent with its sign like "18%"; the market's default, 0.18 for CREDIT, at most the market's max trigger), trigger_ltv for protect (by the market's rule; CREDIT: the target plus 7 points, at least 0.27 and at most 0.3), allow (addresses borrowed USDG may go to, 16 at most), gas_station (true: put the agent's gas station on the allowlist), bills (true: bill pay, the agent's own wallet on the allowlist, for x402 bills through credit_bill; the daily limit then defaults to $100), keeper ("borro", the default, "none" or an address), sell_bps and slip_bps for protect's sales (CREDIT defaults 2500 and 300; 0 in a market with no pool). Check each transaction's to: the factory, a line the factory confirms (isAccount), or the credit for an exact approval. Policy credit: when the agent has claimed a policy in the registry and the line has a gas station or bill pay, its default daily limit is the policy's earned default for the claim's rung (the policy tool shows it) whenever that is more, capped by the ceiling, and daily_limit_note names the policy, its tier and the rung.

tools.name: account_open
tools.title: Prepare: open a trade account
tools.description: Unsigned transaction opening the wallet's version 2 trade account (a TradeAccountV2, one per owner, made by TradeAccountFactoryV2): a trade account with Bailouts, where the owner may post standing offers that pay rescuers to save a position instead of letting it be liquidated (bailout_offer). An agent may be named: an optional second key, never the wallet itself, that can open and close positions within its slippage of the stock's feed, set triggers and cancel the ones it set, post offers within the owner's cap, and send money out to the owner alone. Positions opened inside the account can carry triggers (stop-loss, take-profit, liquidation guard) that anyone can execute for a tip once the price feed confirms them; positions opened from the wallet cannot (close them and open them again inside). Whenever no bailout is owed the owner can take everything out at any time and nobody, Borro included, can stop that; while one is owed, the owner's way out is to pay it (bailout_repay), which lifts the lien at once. A version 1 account the wallet holds stays as it is and keeps working; the other trade tools take either. With a version 2 account open already: agent names a new agent (the old agent's triggers and offers are cancelled with it), revoke_agent: true revokes it at once; account names which of the wallet's accounts to change (default its version 2 one). The owner's settings, on a new account or an open one: the agent's limits (agent_slip_bps, agent_max_tip_bps, agent_max_margin_usdg, agent_daily_loss_usdg, agent_restricted; the agent opens nothing, takes no deposit out, sets no trigger and posts no offer until it has a daily loss budget, and closes whatever the budget; it tips nothing until it has a max tip), agent_bailout_max_usdg (the most an agent's offer may put at stake, 0 by default: none) and max_slip_bps, how far a stop's or a guard's fire bound may widen past its slip (while an offer is live or a bailout is owed it may come down and never up). Simulated from the wallet.

tools.title: Prepare: trade through the trade account
tools.description: Unsigned transactions to open or close a short or a leveraged long through the trade account: the same trades as open_short, close_short, open_long and close_long, with the account as the trader. action open_short (symbol, amount, deposit), close_short (symbol: all of the account's short on it), open_long (symbol, margin, leverage) or close_long (symbol, percent). The account pays from its own USDG; when it holds too little, a USDG transfer from the wallet to the account comes before the trade (from the agent's wallet with fund_from_wallet: true alone, since the agent's own USDG then becomes the owner's and can go out to the owner alone, never back to the agent). What a close returns stays in the account as USDG (account_withdraw takes it out). The wallet must be the account's owner or its agent; the agent's trades must price within its slippage of the stock's feed (refused in words when the pool is further off). The agent's opens need room in the daily loss budget the owner set: refused in words when it is 0 or today's loss has reached it (until 00:00 UTC), and by the account when the open's own shortfall against the feed would pass it. Its closes run whatever the budget (any share, within its slip), counted into today's loss, past the budget by at most their own shortfall. The answer says how much of the budget is left.

tools.name: trigger_set
tools.title: Prepare: set a stop-loss, take-profit or liquidation guard
tools.description: Unsigned transaction leaving an order on a position in the trade account, which anyone may execute once the price feed confirms it, for a tip. kind stop (stop-loss: a short's fires at or above price, a long's at or below), take (take-profit: the other way) or guard (liquidation guard: fires when the position's LTV, Morpho's own at the market's oracle, reaches ltv and closes just enough to bring it down to target; target under ltv under the position's LLTV). A stop or take closes percent of the position (default 100). slip_bps: the most the close may come in worse than the feed's price once the trigger is armed and its bound has widened (100 to 300, default 100; the agent's at most its own limit). tip_bps: the executor's tip, a share of the closed notional at the feed, capped (tip_bps, at most 50 basis points, and never more than the USDG the close returns) (default: the smallest that covers a fire's gas at today's gas and ETH prices, at least 10 from the owner; the agent's at most its max tip, 0 unless the owner set one). The answer says who will fire it: Borro's keeper fires a trigger whose tip covers its fire's gas (taken as 1,100,000 gas until the keeper screens the fire). A trigger whose tip does not cover its fire's gas (a zero tip included, any kind; an agent's trigger pays no tip past its daily loss budget until 00:00 UTC) is fired by Borro's keeper from its root owner's low-tip allowance alone: 0.0001 ETH of gas a UTC day (a few fires), its owner's alone. At most 40 root owners hold one a UTC day, by spending from it: a free one goes to a trigger that is ready and about to be fired, and to no other, in the keeper's owner order (a fire on record, then the least keeper work today, then the oldest trade account) and while its owner is under 200 units of keeper work that day, so the owners whose triggers fire earliest may take all 40 that day. Past it, the trigger is left to other executors. A close under $5 (dust) is left to other executors whatever the tip. Borro's keeper charges all its work on a trigger (screens, checks and simulations, 1 unit each; arms and resets, 5) to the trigger's root owner until the trigger fires, when it is given back. tools.name: policy
tools.title: Policy credit: a policy's record, or a wallet's claim
tools.description: Policy credit: an agent's borrowing terms follow the record of the code it runs (its policy: the content hash of code, model and prompt), across every wallet that claims it. Pass policy (a hash) for its ledger entry, or wallet for its claim and that policy's entry: the tier (newborn, proven or established, from the lines, repayments, liquidations and bad debt of every wallet that claims it), the earned default daily limit by rung, and the honest limits of each rung. Rung 0: a signature from the wallet ("I run policy H"), checked by nobody, defaults up to 250 USDG a day. Rung 1: a hardware attestation (a dstack TEE quote) that the wallet's key lives in an enclave running image H, verified off chain by Borro's keeper, which attests on chain; the raw quote is public, so anyone can re-verify; up to 500. Rung 2: a zk proof per action (SP1) that the action is what program H outputs on committed inputs, checked by the SP1 verifier contract at the registry; up to 1,000. Honest limits: rung 0 proves nothing (a lying wallet poisons the policy it claimed, and the policy's owner can disown it); rung 1 trusts the chip maker and the enclave operator, and Borro's keeper is the on-chain attester (the quote itself is published, so the keeper cannot invent one); rung 2 serves policies that are pure functions over Borro's public inputs, which no LLM-driven agent is; nothing proves which weights a closed model used.
